messages:
sam_support: FYI customer (acme-ai) reporting intermittent 504s + 5xxs from hosted API starting ~09:12 UTC. They see p95 token latency spike and some requests timing out at the gateway. attaching their repro and a sample curl.

alice.nguyen: I'm seeing a correlated alert: `hosted.gateway.p95 > 2s` and `hosted.queue.depth >= 1200` across 3 zones. dashboard: https://console.redwood.example.com/d/queues/hosted-overview

ben_k: logs show gateway returning upstream 504 and a lot of `queue_wait_timeout` traces. snippet from gateway logs:
```
2026-03-15T09:13:05Z ERROR gateway request_id=xyz upstream=svc-hosted-1 status=504 reason="batcher timeout" queue_depth=1278
2026-03-15T09:13:06Z WARN  batcher id=pool-3 wait_ms=1200 backlog=420 pending_requests=640
```

cora-ops: continuous-batcher backlog looks like it's not draining. we've got a mix of very long sequence requests and small ones; backlog is causing big tail latency. p99 token timeouts line up with `kv-cache-evict` churn: when cache evicts, each large request pays cold KV cost and stalls batching. hypothesis: tenant ramped up long-seq streaming requests which break batching efficiency.

sam_support: customer says they didn't change their traffic pattern intentionally. they sent us this curl that reproduces the 504 when looped quickly:
```
for i in `seq 1 200`; do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    -d '{"model":"gptx-large","input":"'$(printf 'word %.0s' {1..200})'","max_tokens":800}' &
done
wait
```

ben_k: repro locally against a staging pool with similar config causes queue depth to climb and then `RequestQueueDepthExceeded` errors once we hit per-host soft limit (we have `max_queue_depth=1500` on hosted by policy). stack traces show the gateway is rejecting only after batchers get saturated, not at ingress.

ingress-bot: auto-scaling triggered +2 workers at 09:14:30 but they weren't enough to collapse the backlog. current scale events: [09:14:30 scale up, 09:15:10 scale up].

deploy-bot: canary rollout for newer batcher kernel is at 20% — not on the nodes showing the worst backlog.

alice.nguyen: mitigation proposals:
- short-term: enable route-level shedding to fallback small-model (cheap) for acme-ai while we investigate
- short-term: reduce `batch_wait_ms` from 40 -> 20 on affected pools to flush smaller batches faster (tradeoff: throughput down, latency down)
- mid-term: raise per-host `max_queue_depth` or enable spillover to dedicated burst nodes
- long-term: add token-length-aware routing so long-seq requests go to dedicated lanes

cora-ops: I pushed a temporary route override to route acme-ai to `gptx-medium-fallback` at 09:17. spike of errors drops immediately. Monitoring: queue depth for acme-ai pool fell from 1300 -> 220 in ~2m. flagging for postmortem.

sam_support: customer confirmed reduced errors after fallback, but wants root cause and remediation. they also asked for statement on SLA impact (they saw ~7% errors over 20m window).

ben_k: reproducer + observations:
- cause: high concurrent long-sequence requests from single tenant causing continuous batcher backlog and heavy KV cache churn
- amplification: default batching settings favor latency for medium-length workloads; when long seq items mix in, batch formation stalls while waiting for long requests to fill.
- gating: per-host `max_queue_depth` kicked in and started rejecting requests -> 5xx/504 seen by client

cora-ops: immediate follow-ups assigned:
- ben_k: gather flamegraphs and batcher metrics for the 09:10-09:25 window and attach to ticket (#INC-4521)
- alice_nguyen: draft customer-facing incident note + mitigation steps and timeline
- infra: evaluate increasing `max_queue_depth` vs enabling tenant-level burst routing

sam_support: repro steps for engineering (please paste into runbook):
1) use the curl loop above or our load-generator `tools/hammer --template longseq --concurrency 200 --duration 5m`
2) watch `hosted.gateway.queue_depth` and `batcher.backlog` in the console
3) inspect gateway logs: filter `reason="batcher timeout"`
4) to reproduce rejection locally set `--max-queue-depth=300` on the gateway binary

alice_nguyen: adding follow-ups to product: defaults should be safer for mixed-length workloads. I'll propose a config change and a new adaptive-batching flag in the next roadmap sync.

ben_k: technical notes I'm attaching in the ticket: snippets, raw flamegraphs, and a minimal reproducer that shows how KV cache cold misses double per-token latency. also noting that canary kernel not being on worst nodes means kernel wasn't the issue.

cora-ops: post-incident mitigation we should:
- instrument tenant-level request-length histogram + alert when >1% of requests > 5k tokens
- add an emergency route fallback API for SRE to quickly send tenants to smaller models
- add an automated temporary-burst mode that routes overflow to a standby worker pool

sam_support: I'll update the customer with the timeline and next steps. thanks everyone. tagging for follow-through :thumbsup:

alice.nguyen: summary for ticket header (to be used in incident mail):
- impact: acme-ai saw ~7% 5xx/504s across a 20m window due to request-queue saturation
- root cause: tenant-generated long-sequence traffic that reduced batching efficiency and caused KV cold misses, leading to continuous-batcher backlog and per-host queue limits being hit
- immediate mitigation: route tenant to fallback model; reduced batch_wait and scaled up workers
- next steps: tenant throttles, config defaults, and routing/observability improvements

ben_k: attaching logs to #INC-4521. will follow up with a PR for an adaptive `batch_wait_ms` experiment.

cora-ops: closing active alerts for now, marking incident as "mitigated". we'll keep watch for 24h.

deploy-bot: rollback planned? none. canary kernel will remain at 20% until next verification window.

sam_support: customer replied: appreciate the fast mitigation, want an ETA for permanent fix. I told them we'll prioritize tenant-level routing and an incident report within 3 working days.

alice.nguyen: good. please add any additional logs or reproduction notes into the ticket and we can start the postmortem draft tomorrow.

--- end of thread ---
